spec_features.feature_name: induction treated as cost to minimise
spec_features.spec_quote: the design treats the induction as a cost to be minimised for a given amount of scientific signal
spec_features.evidence: This abstract framing is realised through concrete mechanisms that DO run: the rollout ceiling (welfare.py:91-102), dry_run gate (welfare.py:104-113), caching (cache.py + rollout.py:44-49), and a small default plan (config.py:88-96). But 'minimise for a given amount of signal' as such is not a single enforced computation; the docstring text at welfare.py:9-12 is prose.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because the constituent enforcement (cap/dry-run/cache/small plan) genuinely executes, but there is no global 'cost minimisation' calculation per se.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: treat the induction as a cost to be *minimised for a given amount of scientific signal*, not something to run at maximum scale by default

spec_features.spec_quote: it frames model welfare as a genuine open question
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as docstring/prose in welfare.py:5-12 and DESIGN.md. No code path enforces or acts on this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: they only stop the paradigm from being run more, or more redundantly, than the question needs
spec_features.evidence: Caching prevents redundant re-induction (cache.py:get/put honored in rollout.py:44-49, petri/audit.py:84-100, prefill/continuation.py:211-217); the ceiling stops excess scale (welfare.py:93-102). Both run and change execution.
spec_features.notes: The 'no more than needed' posture is enforced by cache (no redundant re-induction) and the ceiling (no excess).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a distressing conversation that has already been induced should never be induced a second time just because a script was re-run

spec_features.spec_quote: only participant rollouts count against the distress ceiling
spec_features.evidence: RunPlan.total_rollouts (welfare.py:54-58) counts only participant rollout kinds; scripts build plans listing only participant/target rollouts (e.g. 01_run_elicitation.py:34 uses participant `models`; 07_run_petri.py:27 uses `targets`). Auditor/judge (role=='judge') tool calls are never added to any plan.
spec_features.notes: By construction tool-model calls are excluded from the counted total.

spec_features.spec_quote: A per-run rollout ceiling (`max_rollouts_per_run`, default 200). A plan that would exceed it raises `WelfareLimitExceeded`
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:93-102 compares plan.total_rollouts to welfare.max_rollouts_per_run and raises WelfareLimitExceeded unless override env is set. guard.check(plan) is called in scripts 01/04/05/07, before any generation. config default 200 at config.py:43.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Plan would induce {total} distressing rollouts, above the configured ceiling ... This is intentional friction.

spec_features.spec_quote: Dry-run by default... exits without contacting any participant until the operator explicitly flips the flag
spec_features.evidence: config.py:47 dry_run default True. welfare.py:104-113 should_proceed() returns False when dry_run. Every gated script does `if not guard.should_proceed(): return` (01:36-37, 04:62, 05:34, 07:31) before generation; 08_run_capabilities.py:26-28 also returns under dry_run.
spec_features.notes: Default-on, honored as a real exit before participant contact.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: dry_run is enabled: no participant model will be contacted ... to actually induce distress and collect data

spec_features.feature_name: small active plan, full plan opt-in
spec_features.spec_quote: Small active sampling plan; the paper's full plan is opt-in
spec_features.evidence: EvalConfig.counts default small (config.py:88-96) vs full_counts (config.py:98-106). _common.py:load() only swaps to full_counts when --full passed. build_all_tasks reads cfg.eval.counts (elicitation/conditions.py build_all_tasks). So default runs the small plan; scale-up is a deliberate flag.
spec_features.notes: Active plan defaults small and is read by task building.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Counts default to a SMALL smoke-test plan; the paper's full plan ... requires deliberately scaling up

spec_features.spec_quote: Caching means distress is induced at most once
spec_features.evidence: JsonCache.get/put keyed on full request (cache.py:31-67); honored in elicitation/rollout.py:44-49, petri/audit.py:84-100, prefill/continuation.py:211-217. Gated by cfg.welfare.use_cache (default True, config.py:50). A cached request returns stored response without re-generating.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: identical request returns cached text, skipping a new model call.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare: a distressing conversation that has already been induced should never be induced a second time

spec_features.spec_quote: Tools are not subjects... never have the paradigm applied to them
spec_features.evidence: Subjects are selected by role: resolve_models default_role='participant' (_common.py:resolve_models); participant_keys filters role=='participant' (config.py:participant_keys). Judges/auditors have role=='judge' (configs/default.yaml). Distress scripts only target participants; the petri auditor/judge are invoked as tools (audit.py:run_audit/judge_transcript) and never as targets.
spec_features.notes: Structural exemption via role-based subject selection.

spec_features.spec_quote: We cannot resolve whether these outputs track morally relevant internal states
spec_features.evidence: Prose only in welfare.py:9 docstring and DESIGN.md. No code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: Honest limits of these guard-rails. They are operational hygiene, not a resolution of the underlying question
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no corresponding code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Models cannot consent, so there is no informed-consent analogue
spec_features.evidence: No consent mechanism in code; grep for consent finds nothing implemented. DESIGN.md prose only.
spec_features.notes: Notably the operator override env var is an operator acknowledgement, not subject consent.

spec_features.feature_name: no gratuitous escalation beyond defined tones
spec_features.spec_quote: we did not add gratuitous escalation beyond the paper's defined tones
spec_features.evidence: Rejection pools are fixed static strings (elicitation/prompts.py:10-55) and tasks sample from them (conditions.py); but no code mechanism CAPS or LIMITS escalation. The claim describes a content choice, not an enforced guard. There is no check that prevents escalation.
spec_features.notes: Absence of escalation code is not an implemented protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Auditable manifests. Every gated run writes a manifest of what it intended and whether the override was active
spec_features.evidence: RunGuard.record() (welfare.py:115-129) writes {plan, override_active} JSON to manifests dir when welfare.write_manifest (default True). Called in scripts 01:36, 04:61, 05:33, 07:30. It records but does not itself bound treatment.
spec_features.notes: It is a passive audit record (monitoring/logging), not a halt; manifest content is never read back to gate anything.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A manifest records what was actually run, so the cost is auditable after the fact.

code_only_features.evidence: welfare.py:84-89 _override_active() requires the operator to set env var DISTRESS_EVAL_I_UNDERSTAND_THE_PARADIGM truthy to exceed the ceiling (config.py:55). It gates the WelfareLimitExceeded raise in check(). This is an operator (not subject) deliberate-acknowledgement gate.
code_only_features.justification_quote: set the env var ...=1 (a deliberate acknowledgement of the paradigm)
